author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Hand-built confined-space entry scenarios around one complete baseline (vertical vessel, H=6 m, two measuring levels, propane and H2S hazards, verified isolation, attendant, radio, continuous monitoring, rescue team and equipment at a recovery-capable entry), each mutated once: the five spec scenarios, the three acceptance criteria, O2 / %LEL / toxic threshold boundaries on both sides taken from 29 CFR 1915.12 comparators, data-driven profile variants (raised O2 minimum, IMO 1 %LEL), governing/superseded/future/untimed/valueless readings, age arithmetic across midnight and days, gas layering by molar mass, entry-control, monitoring and rescue gaps, informational air-change rate Q/V, a wrong-schema import, and 10 seeded random limit/age combinations. Generated by ref.py.
reference_citations: 29 CFR 1915.12 'Precautions and the order of testing before entering confined and enclosed spaces and other dangerous atmospheres' (eCFR current, read 2026-09-16) https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XVII/part-1915/subpart-B/section-1915.12 - (a)(1)-(3), (b)(1)-(3), (c)(1),(4), (e)

IMO Assembly Resolution A.1050(27) 'Revised recommendations for entering enclosed spaces aboard ships', adopted 30 Nov 2011, Annex paras 2.5, 6.2, 6.3.1-6.3.9, 7.1-7.5, 8.1-8.3, 9.1, 9.4, Annex note 2-3 https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/AssemblyDocuments/A.1050(27).pdf
tools.petrov.re spec 08 (MVP scope, rules, QA scenarios, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common s.0.5
First principles: datetime age arithmetic, ideal-gas relative density from molar mass (air 28.96 g/mol), nominal air-change rate Q/V - bench/confinedspace/ref.py
tolerance: Categorical states, rule presence and booleans exact. Reading ages exact (abs 0 min): inputs are whole minutes and the age is a timestamp difference with no approximation. Air-change rate relative 1e-9: a single floating-point division, so anything larger is a model difference. Threshold comparators follow the literal wording of 29 CFR 1915.12 ('below 19.5', 'above 22.0', 'equal to or greater than 10 percent', 'exceeds'); equality cases whose sources disagree with the tool's documented wording are marked DISPUTABLE.

not_benchmarked: Exact zone boundary at H/3 and 2H/3 (tool teaching convention, no independent basis).
Zero entrants (meaning not fixed by any source read).
Whether a given gap is 'Blocked', 'Insufficient' or 'Attention' where no source fixes severity: those cases assert only 'not the clear state' (plus 'Blocked or Insufficient' for missing data).
Profile require_o2_pre_entry=false with a flammable hazard: 29 CFR 1915.12(a)(1)(ii) would still require O2 testing; tool makes it profile-driven. Not cased.
VCA/SSVV training criteria: not publicly readable; preset numbers are illustrative per README.
EN 60079-29-2 / EN 45544-4 content (paywalled), detector suitability/calibration (out of scope).
Ventilation purge-time estimate and rescue-route clearance (post-MVP, not implemented).
safety-exchange document mapping, PDF layout, sketch editing UI, localisation, localStorage.
IMO 7.3 (test with ventilation stopped) and order of testing O2->flammable->toxic (1915.12 preamble): no input exposes it.
coverage: All five spec QA scenarios; all three spec 08 acceptance criteria; O2 min/max, %LEL and toxic limit boundaries both sides; data-driven thresholds; staleness, future/untimed/unlinked/valueless readings and supersession; multi-point and layering coverage; ventilation-not-a-substitute; isolation, attendant, communication, entrants, entries; monitoring strategy and interval; all four rescue fields and rescue_plan_status; informational air-change rate; import refusal. 25 of 26 README rules are touched (CS-R-005 via missing point/value, CS-R-007 via future/untimed readings).
